newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the second session running and analysts saw them extending gains on Monday, recovering earlier moderate losses amid a longer-term horizontal trend.
"There is a chance for a good beginning of the (next) week, the market should react to its recent falls," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Baring Securities.

Analysts said firming zloty should also help but in the longer-term the bourse was likely to maintain its 12-week horizontal trend with buying limited by the heavy primary market offer and forthcoming general elections due in September.
The main market's WIG index rose 139.1 points, or 0.9 percent, to 15,941.7, and turnover rose 17 percent to 124.4 million zlotys on all three markets as 62 issues rose, 24 fell and 17 were flat.
The bourse fell a total 4.5 percent late last week and early this week amid large offers on the primary market and falling zloty, spurred by the Czech crown slump.

Analysts said the strengthening of the zloty on Friday was a good sign but said its positive impact on the bourse was likely to be limited with capital drawn to the primary market where Bank Handlowy was offering shares worth one billion zlotys.
Analysts said some stocks looked very attractive after recent falls and they expected them to help the bourse rise to at least 16.500 points next week.
